Q: Mapping image brightness to a fixed set of user-selected colors in WinForms A:

You can refactor the if/else part to a switch statement. There is good explanation and example that fits your use case here: Switch case: can I use a range instead of a one number

Not that there is anything particularly wrong with what you already have. It may be a little verbose but it is easy to follow and understand. Changing to a switch statement is unlikely to make any difference to how fast it runs.

For info, questions such as these (with respect to your first question about the if/else at least) are often better posted on the Code Review stack exchange site. Strictly speaking they are out of scope here and likely to get closed.

https://codereview.stackexchange.com/

Q: PHP Script not timing out while using curl_exec( ) A:

It is probably not as elegant as you hope, but, what do you think of, instead of making the main curl fail quickly in the event of a DDoS, trying something likea lightweight preparatory diagnostic before the curl? I ask because other utilities apart from curl/HTTP can be more lightweight in terms of network, for example, a system("ping -c <host>")) whose result can be examined before attempting the curl? (ping has a -t option as well) ... I suppose system() has a cost on the local system too so the tradeoff might not be worth it. Maybe this idea will jog your better ideas ... Either way, I hope you get that elegant suggestion you are seeking 🙏

Q: OpenCV unable to read uncompressed AVI video files in python even though it can open and read metadata A:

First I would suggest modifying your code to something like:

import sys
import cv2

video_path = '/Users/aravind/Downloads/test.avi'  
cap = cv2.VideoCapture(video_path)

print(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FOURCC))
frame_count = cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS)
print("FPS:", frame_count)
print(f"Frame count: {frame_count}")
print("Width:", cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH)) 
print("Height:", cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT))

if not cap.isOpened():
    sys.exit(f"Capture not initialised possible unsupported codac! {video_path}")

work_to_do = (frame_count > 0)
current_frame = 0
while work_to_do:
    current_frame += 1
    print(f"Reading from {current_frame} of {frame_count}", end=" ")
    ok, frame = cap.read()
    if ok:
        print(f" - Read {frame.nbytes=}")
    work_to_do = ok and (current_frame < frame_count)
print(f"Ended after {current_frame} frames!")

So you can see when it "crashes" - the first frame, last or trying to read beyond last.

The reason that this is important is that your current test cap.isOpened() returns True if the initialisation was successful - which you already get a good feel of from the meta data. I suspect that your crash may be because you are trying to read beyond the end of the video file.

If it is crashing at the first frame this means that the Codac was not detected (hence the 0.0) and the default does not work you can try to set the Codec to an appropriate value.

Running my above code on your test.avi file I am able to read all 30 frames with each frame being 110,592 bytes. However, running your code, with the while cap.isOpened(): loop limit, the loop does not terminate but after 60 frames the frame is None so accessing any methods/variables on it will fail with an appropriate error.

Q: I didn't understand why first code is working and second one not? A:

Arrow functions with implicit return. There's an assignment obj[value.id] = value which returns value instead of the desired. Using .reduce() you might want to return the obj accumulator, or in that single-line fashion, like:

=> (obj[value.id] = value, obj), {} );

const users = [
  {id:"a", name:"aa", age:20},
  {id:"b", name:"bb", age:21},
  {id:"c", name:"cc", age:22},
];

const groupById = arr => arr.reduce((acc, user) => (acc[user.id] = user, acc), {});

console.log(groupById(users));

In the above (*** , acc) evaluation, the Accumulator acc Object is now correctly returned.
